extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemakers and regulatory analysts, environmental advocates, industry technical staff, and public commenters on NESHAP/MACT for oil & gas
extracted.subtask_description: Public-interest technical comments critiquing EPA's MACT/technology review and supporting analyses for oil & gas source categories; identifies deficiencies in assumptions, scope, data, and proposes specific control options and regulatory requirements. Intended to guide EPA's notice-and-comment rulemaking record and technical justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide empirical basis for assumed control efficiencies and cost equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assumed that second control devices (condenser or combustion device) achieve at least a 95% HAP reduction and that the costs for the second device were assumed to be equal to the costs of the first device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why 95% was used rather than higher efficiencies (e.g., 98% or 99%), analyze cost-effectiveness impacts of higher efficiencies, and justify any assumption that second-device costs equal first-device costs given dependence on process size, waste-gas volume, and contaminant concentration. Provide supporting data and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify the 95% control assumption for cover + closed vent systems
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA states that sources achieving MACT were assumed to have storage vessels equipped with a cover vented through a closed vent system to a control device which achieves at least a 95% HAP reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical support or references for the 95% control figure (cover + closed vent), and clarify how residual emissions after that control were estimated and whether greater control efficiencies were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support assumptions about HAP/VOC fraction in fugitive emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA asserted that HAP present is approximately 1/20 the VOC present in material handled by regulated equipment and therefore LDAR cost-effectiveness for HAP reduction is ~20x greater than for VOC reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply data demonstrating the HAP-to-VOC ratio for the relevant fugitive sources; if data are poor, perform sensitivity analysis and document uncertainty. Do not rely on unsupported blanket fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and apply “development” broadly for MACT technology review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA defined a 'development' as any add-on control not identified previously; improvements in add-on control technology; any work practice or operational procedure not previously identified; and any process change or pollution prevention alternative that could be broadly applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this broad definition to search widely for developments; do not apply the term narrowly. The review should capture add-on techs, practice changes, and pollution prevention alternatives even if applicability varies across facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a broad, multi-source technology review (not limited to RBLC and NG STAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA appears to have limited its search for 'developments' to the RBLC and Natural Gas STAR documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand the search to vendor literature, state and local regulation, permit and technology review documents, discussions with vendors, and direct engagement with facilities. Document search dates and methods, and include summaries in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize and analyze Natural Gas STAR program findings in the docket
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's docket memo listed the RBLC summary but provided no substantive summary or analysis of Natural Gas STAR despite stating it was reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a documented summary of NG STAR demonstrations, quantify the emissions reductions achieved, and explain how NG STAR experience informs MACT options and stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and use facility-level best-practice data
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA did not attempt to collect data reflecting best practices at facilities and relied on limited correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect primary data on best practices from facilities, vendors, and state programs; use case studies and post-MACT demonstrations to update analyses and potential standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider state and local regulations and technology requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: States such as California, Colorado, and Wyoming have regulated many sources at more stringent levels than EPA's proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and incorporate state rules (e.g., BAAQMD Reg. 8, Rule 18; CO and WY low/no-bleed and green completion requirements) and explain how these more-stringent state measures affect MACT feasibility and stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and review vendor literature and state permit technology analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA failed to conduct a broad-based search of vendor literature addressing control methods and approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include vendor brochures, equipment specifications (compressor seals, pneumatic devices, combustion control devices, flares, valves, flanges), state permit technology reviews, and rulemaking support documents to identify feasible controls and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not dismiss technologies as 'unproven' solely for not applying to all units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA dismissed several Natural Gas STAR technologies as 'new and unproven' or not applicable to all glycol dehydrators and therefore not MACT options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technologies on demonstrated performance where applicable; consider partial applicability or use for new sources; Section 112(d)'s purpose is to drive technology forward—do not exclude options simply because they cannot be applied universally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require justification when rejecting control options (e.g., leak detection, compressor fixes)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA rejected options like directed inspection and maintenance, ultrasonic leak detection, compressor rod packing replacement, and dry-seal replacement citing reasons (cost criteria, inability to quantify, low HAP content) without adequate support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear evidence when rejecting options: demonstrate inability to quantify leaks via ultrasonic methods, clarify what 'low HAP content' means numerically, and show cost/emissions calculations supporting rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify statements of 'comparability' for storage vessel technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA stated Natural Gas STAR technologies for storage vessels are 'comparable' to cover+control technologies in MACT, implying no additional HAP reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'comparable' quantitatively, provide comparisons of estimated emissions reductions, and justify why NG STAR options would or would not materially increase HAP reductions beyond current MACT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate glycol dehydrator alternative compliance option of 0.9 Mg/yr benzene
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as a 112(f) risk reduction option for Oil and Natural Gas Production and for Natural Gas Transmission and Storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider regulatory removal of the 0.9 Mg/yr benzene alternative compliance pathway to ensure stricter HAP control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a second control device on glycol dehydrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Identified as a 112(f) risk-reduction option for Oil and Natural Gas Production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate feasibility, associated control efficiency gains (including >95% options), and costs for requiring a second control device on dehydrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a second control device on storage tanks
rubrics_metrics.description: Identified as a 112(f) risk-reduction option and discussed as an investigated option (cover + control device, then add-on combustion device assumed 95% reduction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze control performance and cost for requiring additional add-on controls (e.g., combustion device achieving higher destruction efficiencies) and provide justification for assumed efficiencies and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require more stringent LDAR programs for leak detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under both 112(f) and 112(d)(6) option lists: require more stringent LDAR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify detection technologies, inspection frequency, repair criteria, and cost-effectiveness metrics for HAP reductions (with appropriate HAP/VOC scaling supported by data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require compliance with 40 CFR part 60 subpart VVa rather than subpart VV plant-wide
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as a 112(f) risk reduction option for Oil and Natural Gas Production and in 112(d)(6) options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze differences in standards between subparts VVa and VV and justify requiring subpart VVa in place of VV where appropriate to achieve greater HAP reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require compliance with 40 CFR part 60 subpart VVa for certain components (instead of VV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as an option to require VVa rather than VV for certain components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific equipment categories where VVa is more protective, quantify emissions benefits, and estimate compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require use of optical gas imaging (OGI) monthly with annual Method 21 check
rubrics_metrics.description: Identified as an option: monthly OGI plus annual EPA Method 21 verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify performance criteria, inspection frequency, and integration with LDAR programs; provide cost and detection efficacy analysis compared to current practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate Natural Gas STAR glygol-dehydrator techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural Gas STAR-listed techniques include: optimize glycol circulation rates; Flash Tank Separator (FTS) installation; electric pump installation; re-route glycol skimmer gas; replace glycol dehydrators with methanol injection; replace with desiccant dehydrators; replace with separators and in-line heaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess applicability, emissions reduction potential (including technologies that achieve zero HAP emissions in some cases), operational constraints (temperature, volume, pressure limits), and cost-effectiveness. Do not dismiss categorically as 'new/unproven' without evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt low or no-bleed pneumatic devices or route discharges to closed-loop systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of low/no-bleed pneumatic devices reduces venting; Colorado and Wyoming require low/no-bleed or routing discharge streams to closed-loop systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requiring low/no-bleed devices where feasible, quantify VOC and HAP reductions and payback periods (noted as <1 year in examples), and reflect state practices in federal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require green (reduced-emission) well completions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use portable or permanent equipment to recover rather than vent gas during final well drilling; Colorado and Wyoming require green completions where feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technical and economic feasibility, applicability criteria, and require green completions unless technically/economically infeasible; quantify methane, VOC, and HAP reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 98% HAP control standard for glycol dehydrators (state precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wyoming requires control of HAPs and VOCs by at least 98% at dehydration units in certain areas regardless of emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a 98% control requirement is feasible for new and existing dehydrators in broader contexts, including costs and availability of technologies that achieve that efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require control of flash emissions from tanks to high destruction (e.g., 98%) and at first production
rubrics_metrics.description: Wyoming requires tanks to control flash emissions upon first date of production and statewide requires 98% control for certain thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine feasibility of requiring flash-emission controls at initial production and adopting high-percentage control (e.g., 98%); consider technology options (adsorbers, oxidizers, floating roofs) and cost implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address production-sector fugitive emissions with a suite of measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Control options include improving operating practices, installing compressor rod packing systems, substituting high-bleed with low-bleed pneumatics, improving leak detection, electronic flare ignition, replacing older equipment, and installing vapor recovery devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bundle and evaluate these measures in LDAR and equipment-replacement programs, quantify emission reductions and costs, and consider regulatory requirements or best-practice standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt plunger lifts and smart well automation for well unloading
rubrics_metrics.description: Plunger lifts and smart automation can remove fluids without venting and improve productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess applicability at mature wells, quantify emission reductions and productivity benefits, and consider as recommended or required practice where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install BASO valves on gas-fired heaters and remote equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: BASO valves automatically shut off gas flow upon pilot flame extinguishment, preventing venting; ideal for remote locations (no electricity required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requiring BASO valves on crude oil heater-treaters, gas dehydrators, and heaters located at exploration and development sites to prevent unnecessary emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and make prior MACT rulemaking materials available in the docket
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA relied on prior MACT development but did not make clear what prior analyses/documents were used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide and cite all prior rulemaking documents used as the basis for current assumptions so reviewers can verify whether earlier matters (e.g., consideration of glycol circulation optimization or flash tank separators) were in fact evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: When scaling LDAR cost-effectiveness from VOC to HAP, provide transparent methodology and data
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA scaled LDAR cost-effectiveness by assuming HAPs are ~1/20 of VOCs, leading to a ~20x greater cost-effectiveness for HAP reduction; record data support is weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the methodology, data sources, and uncertainty bounds for scaling; conduct sensitivity analyses and do not rely on unsupported ratios.
